source.title: Synergistic Network Learning and Label Correction for Noise-Robust Image Classification
source.authors: Chen Gong; B. Kong; E. Seibel; Xin Wang; You-Bing Yin; Qi Song

record.tranche_reason: The study reports test accuracy for standard deep-network baselines across synthetic label-noise rates, a different measure relevant to the test-error component of V4. It does not report training error.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy for its Standard baseline on noisy labels, but no training-error results. Its statements about learning patterns before fitting noise and its discussion of dropout are background, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The method relies on V6's real-patterns-before-noise premise to select small-loss examples and correct labels. Its own experiments evaluate noise mitigation, without measuring training-label memorization or the learning order of clean and noisy examples. Section 3.3 states that the Standard baseline results are quoted from reference [16], so their declining test accuracy is not this study's own test of V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion that their method performs well against baselines on synthetic and real-world noisy-label datasets. Their overall-winner claim needs the reported qualification: on Clothing1M, their method has the best validation-selected test accuracy, but its final-epoch accuracy is 0.05 percentage points below LDM I.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses synthetic symmetric and asymmetric label corruption, with a Standard deep-network baseline and a proposed method that jointly trains two networks and corrects labels. It does not reproduce the random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies across the reported symmetric label-noise rates and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed method improves test accuracy by selecting examples and correcting their labels; its ablations compare correction intervals and retraining. These measure mitigation performance, not fitting the original noisy labels or learning clean labels before noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Combining small-loss selection with intermittent label correction can improve classification accuracy under label noise.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
record.problems: The study reports test accuracy but no training error for the Standard baseline; therefore it cannot establish whether the baseline fits its noisy training labels. The Standard baseline results are reported over five trials for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, but no uncertainty is given for the Clothing1M results.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the reported Standard-baseline test accuracies under synthetic label noise do not establish the combined V4 outcome, which also requires perfect training fit. Table 1 reports CIFAR-10; Table 2 reports CIFAR-100; Table 3 reports Clothing1M.

untested.parts: Near-zero training error on completely random labels, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and training hyperparameters.
Relative training time for true and random labels and convergence speed as corruption increases.
Training fit on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

The study supplies no own standard-network results establishing perfect training fit alongside steadily worsening test error across corruption rates. Standard-baseline accuracies are quoted; zero and complete corruption are not evaluated.
Whether explicit regularization prevents random-label fitting or is necessary for generalization on true labels.
The temporal order of learning real patterns and memorizing noisy labels is used as a premise, without a direct measurement.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's tests/T2 classification overlooks the attribution of Standard-baseline results to reference [16]. No claim-relevant result rows need adding: the quoted baseline results are already declared in rows_left_out, and the study's own mitigation results do not establish any claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Random labels, training error, test error at chance, and unchanged architecture or hyperparameters are not tested.
Training time and convergence as label-noise fraction changes are not reported.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs are not tested.

Test accuracy under some symmetric label-noise rates is reported for the Standard baselines, but the study does not report whether training error remains zero, does not test a 100% corruption condition, and does not establish a steady progression across the full range from no corruption to all labels corrupted.
The study does not test whether weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation affect random-label fitting or true-label generalization.
The study cites prior work on learning patterns before memorizing noise but does not test the learning order of real and random labels.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
